title: Record the denied command, not just the tool name
lead: Seen 2026-10-20: the run record keeps only 'Bash' for each denial, so the owner cannot tell which command was denied or fix the allowlist. Claude's result lists the denied command (permission_denials[].tool_input.command; fixture testdata/vendors/claude/04-allowlist-denies-write.stdout). Record it on the role, show it in ork status and the TUI detail, and bound its length. Take care: a command may contain secrets, so cap and note this.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- Decided #105 (engine.denied-command): RoleRecord.Denials stays the tool names; a new optional omitempty field holds {tool, command} entries. Record Version stays 1.
- A denied Bash call records its command; any other denied tool records tool_input.file_path when present, never file content.
- CR and LF in the text become spaces. Text over 200 characters is cut to 197 plus '...' so the result is at most 200.
- ork status and the TUI detail show it inline per denial, for example 'denied: Bash: git push origin main, Write: /x.txt'. A denial with no detail reads 'Write'.
- The stop reason (engine round.go) names the same text.
- Existing run records without commands still load.
- docs/state.md says a recorded command can hold secrets: it is capped, not scrubbed. A pre-S45 ork refuses a run.json that holds a command.
